:::{#def-gradient-linear-approximation}
#### Linear approximation of the gradient

Let $f$ be as in [Newton's method](#def-newton-method) and let $\vx$ be a point.
The **linear approximation of the gradient** of $f$ at $\vx$
is the $p \times 1$ [vector-valued function](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-vector-valued) $\lingrad$ of a step $\stepvec \in \reals^p$
whose $j$th entry, for $j = 1, \ldots, p$,
is the function whose [graph](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-graph) is the [tangent plane](#def-tangent-plane) to the graph of the [partial derivative](vector-calculus.qmd#def-partial-derivative) $\deriv{x_j} f$ at $\vx$,
evaluated at $\vx + \stepvec$:

$$
\sb{\lingradf{\stepvec}}_j \eqdef \deriv{x_j} f(\vx) + \tp{\paren{\deriv{\vx} \paren{\deriv{x_j} f(\vx)}}} \stepvec.
$$ {#eq-gradient-linear-approximation}

:::
